page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-1 is an arm64-based virtual machine instance belonging to the n4a server family. It features 1 dedicated vCPU and 4.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, relying on network-attached storage options for persistent disk requirements.

The dedicated arm64 CPU architecture provides predictable compute performance for entry-level workloads without the resource sharing or CPU credit limitations typical of burstable instances. The 4.0 GB of RAM per core offers a balanced environment for lightweight applications. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4a-standard-1 represents a low-cost entry point into the GCP ARM ecosystem, offering dedicated resources at a minimal hardware profile.

This instance is suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, including small-scale web serving, microservices, development environments, and basic utility scripting. Due to its single-core configuration and lack of local storage or GPU acceleration, it is not intended for heavy database operations, parallel processing, or machine learning workloads.
